crossPairDispositions.acceptedPrompt: A listing stores price and stock. The market’s policy rejects publication when either is invalid; the publish page currently fetches fields and branches before setting Published. Choose how publication should be invoked so every entry point enforces the same rule.
crossPairDispositions.candidatePrompt: A produce marketplace publishes a listing after its price and stock are checked. Listing owns its price, stock, and visibility. The publish controller currently checks both values and then flips visibility; a second caller skips the stock check. In this case, which design decision addresses the behavior’s placement without moving unrelated orchestration?
crossPairDispositions.acceptedKey: Ask Listing.publish() to validate its price and stock before changing its status.
crossPairDispositions.candidateKey: Make Listing’s publish operation validate its own price and stock before becoming visible.
crossPairDispositions.rationale: The regional listing/price-stock publication facts and owner-validation action are materially the same as the accepted N02 item; the current stem only changes wording and adds a second-caller detail that the accepted item already generalized to every entry point. The N09 unit objective (misplaced behavior/feature envy) is not independently tested by this exact repeat.

crossPairDispositions.acceptedPrompt: An escalation desk raises a conversation to a specialist queue. The assigned owner and response deadline must change in the same accepted escalation; a separate activity feed may update afterward. Which boundary should own acceptance?
crossPairDispositions.candidatePrompt: In A customer-support escalation desk, An escalation changes assignee and response deadline together. Two agents can act on a conversation at nearly the same time, and the customer-visible record must not pair one agent's assignment with another action's deadline. Which operation boundary best preserves these facts?
crossPairDispositions.acceptedKey: Commit owner and deadline as one conversation transition.
crossPairDispositions.candidateKey: Apply assignee and deadline in one current conversation transition.
crossPairDispositions.rationale: Both use escalation owner/deadline facts and a conversation transition. N08 adds two near-simultaneous agents and a mixed-assignment/deadline failure that N07 does not contain; the item reinforces the aggregate boundary with an explicit concurrency trigger, so repetition is purposeful.

crossPairDispositions.acceptedPrompt: An annotation editor accepts a comment. The comment must retain the author and document revision; a notification is sent only after the comment is committed. If the notification provider is unavailable, the accepted comment remains valid. What is the appropriate save sequence?
crossPairDispositions.candidatePrompt: In A collaborative annotation workspace, A comment is accepted against one author and document revision. Notification can fail after acceptance; retry must send the accepted comment identity without changing what was committed. Which change should become visible as one coherent state?
crossPairDispositions.acceptedKey: Commit the comment and author/revision links before separate notification.
crossPairDispositions.candidateKey: Commit the comment identity and revision before emitting its retryable notification.
crossPairDispositions.rationale: Both use accepted comment metadata before notification. N08 additionally asks for retry of the already accepted identity without changing committed state after notification failure; that case-specific retry boundary is absent from N07, so this is a supported transfer/reinforcement rather than an identical decision.

crossPairDispositions.acceptedPrompt: In a digital invoice exchange, the billing operator must reissue a rejected invoice. The new issue is traceable and does not double-charge the customer. Each invoice issue has an issue ID. Delivery retry repeats that issue ID; a corrected reissue gets a new issue ID and points to the rejected issue. How should the service distinguish retry from reissue?
crossPairDispositions.candidatePrompt: In a digital invoice exchange, each issue has a stable issue ID; the exchange may accept it before the response is lost. Finance can correct and reissue an invoice after reconciling the first, and must avoid charging the same issue twice. Which retry policy should the client use?
crossPairDispositions.acceptedKey: Retry uses the existing issue ID; corrected reissue is a new issue record with a new ID and a link to the rejected one.
crossPairDispositions.candidateKey: Look up this issue ID’s outcome; treat a corrected reissue as a separate invoice issue.
crossPairDispositions.rationale: Both concern invoice issue IDs and a corrected reissue. N02 states the original invoice is known rejected and teaches existing ID for delivery retry versus a new linked ID for reissue. N08 asks how to reconcile a possibly accepted issue after a lost response before corrected reissue. The uncertain-ack outcome is a distinct decisive fact and allows legitimate reinforcement; no exactly-once guarantee is claimed.
